biography: Pedro Park, the 'Celtic Comet,' hails from the small coastal town of Ballycotton, Ireland. His racing journey began at age 10, tearing around the family farm on a modified lawnmower, much to the chagrin of his father. What started as youthful rebellion quickly morphed into a burning passion. A defining moment came at 14, during a local karting championship; despite starting last due to a mechanical issue, Pedro clawed his way to victory, showcasing raw talent and an unyielding spirit. Now at 17, Pedro is making waves in the junior single-seater circuit, attracting attention with his flamboyant style and daring overtakes, all while navigating the challenges of being an independent driver.
drivingStyle: Pedro's driving style is a high-risk, high-reward affair. He's known for his late-braking maneuvers and aggressive corner entries, often pushing the limits of grip. Tire management isn't exactly his forte; he tends to burn through rubber quickly in pursuit of lap times. Under pressure, Pedro thrives, relishing the opportunity to make daring passes and secure crucial positions, though sometimes this impulsiveness leads to costly mistakes.

rivalries.reason: A clash of personalities and driving styles. Alessandro is calculated and precise, directly contrasting Pedro's 'send it' mentality, leading to several on-track collisions and heated exchanges.
A battle for sponsorship and recognition. Both rising stars are vying for limited opportunities, creating a fierce competition both on and off the track.
A rivalry stemming from a controversial incident where Kenji claimed Pedro unfairly blocked him during a crucial qualifying lap, costing him a front-row start.

quirks: Always wears a lucky green shamrock bracelet given to him by his grandmother before every race.
Insists on listening to traditional Irish folk music on full blast in the garage before getting into the car.
Has a habit of sketching race tracks in the dirt with his finger while strategizing.
famousQuote: "I don't race to finish second. I race to win, or I race to crash trying. Either way, it'll be a good show!"
careerHighlight: Winning the Junior Formula Ireland Championship in his debut season, securing the title with a spectacular last-lap overtake that cemented his reputation as a fearless racer.
careerLowPoint: Crashing out of the lead in the final race of the Formula Atlantic series due to a misjudged overtaking attempt, costing him a potential podium finish and valuable championship points.
